policy: Append material failures and contingencies. Resolved entries remain historical evidence and are not deleted merely because the project later passes.

entries.symptom: The locked main-branch dependency graph reports one low and three high vulnerability entries.
entries.expected: The release dependency graph has no unresolved high-severity advisory entry.
entries.actual: npm audit reports high-severity entries for Next.js 16.2.4 and its PostCSS/sharp dependency paths, plus a low-severity esbuild development-server entry. npm identifies Next.js 16.3.3 as the non-major fix path.
quarantine_scope: release-readiness claims for the main-branch dependency graph
remaining_uncertainty: Runtime exploitability was not individually assessed in the API_SE_001 documentation/discovery mutation cone.
The available Next.js 16.3.3 update still needs exact-head type, lint, test, build and audit proof after convergence with current work.
entries.next_action: Converge the existing dependency-update pull requests or an equivalent Next.js 16.3.3 lockfile update, then rerun the full release gate and npm audit on the exact candidate SHA.

entries.symptom: Initial read-only Docker container discovery could not access the desktop Docker socket from the default sandbox.
entries.expected: Read-only discovery identifies whether a disposable Postgres restore target is available.
entries.actual: The sandbox returned permission denied for the Docker socket; the approved escalated read-only command identified local Postgres 16 containers.
repair_attempts: Reran the same read-only discovery with explicit sandbox approval.
remaining_uncertainty: Desktop Docker availability does not prove production recovery infrastructure.
entries.next_action: Retain explicit authorization for future disposable drills and never infer provider backup access from local Docker.

entries.symptom: The first fingerprint attempt failed before backup/target creation because psql autocommit dropped the temporary count table.
entries.expected: The session-scoped temporary table remains available to the PL/pgSQL scan and final aggregate query.
entries.actual: ON COMMIT DROP removed the table immediately after CREATE TEMP TABLE in autocommit mode; cleanup verified the named target did not exist.
evidence_refs: first drill stderr: relation recovery_table_counts does not exist
repair_attempts: Removed ON COMMIT DROP so the temporary table remains for the psql session.
remaining_uncertainty: The passing repair proves the local logical drill only.
entries.next_action: Keep the failed attempt referenced by every API_SE_014 proof and retain the fingerprint mismatch gate.

entries.symptom: The first recovery test used the regular-expression dot-all flag, which is newer than the repository TypeScript target.
entries.expected: New tests compile under the repository's current TypeScript target.
entries.actual: TypeScript TS1501 rejected the dot-all flag before test execution.
repair_attempts: Replaced dot-all with the target-compatible [\s\S] expression.
entries.next_action: Preserve the repository target in future contract-test syntax.

entries.symptom: The first production build warned that the shared telemetry module imported node:crypto in an Edge-runtime bundle.
entries.expected: Shared telemetry semantics compile for every Next.js runtime that imports instrumentation/catalog code.
entries.actual: Tenant hashing pulled node:crypto into the Edge graph; the same sandboxed build also hit the already-known external Google Font fetch boundary.
evidence_refs: first API_SE_008 npm run build output
repair_attempts: Removed tenant hashing and omitted tenant/actor identity entirely from shared telemetry.
deferred_external_infra: Sandboxed Google Font fetch; rerun requires network access and is not telemetry capability evidence.
remaining_uncertainty: No Edge deployment or telemetry exporter was exercised.
entries.next_action: Keep the shared telemetry module runtime-neutral and perform exporter-specific crypto only in explicitly Node-owned adapters.

entries.symptom: The initial invalid-target test received the event-count error first and could not independently prove the target-ratio guard.
entries.expected: A known-bad target ratio fails through its explicit target-ratio boundary.
entries.actual: The fixture also had badEvents greater than totalEvents, and count validation ran before target validation.
repair_attempts: Validated targetRatio before event counts and retained explicit fail-closed guards for both input classes.
entries.next_action: Retain independent negative fixtures for target ratios and bounded event counts.

entries.symptom: The default sandbox could not fetch the configured Geist and Geist Mono Google Font stylesheets during the production build.
entries.expected: The exact implementation commit completes the production build gate.
entries.actual: Turbopack failed only at restricted external font fetch; the approved network-enabled rerun compiled, typechecked and generated all routes successfully.
repair_attempts: Reran the unchanged build with approved network access to the configured font provider.
remaining_uncertainty: The build continues to depend on font-provider availability when the artifacts are not already cached.
entries.next_action: Preserve the network boundary in build evidence; evaluate self-hosted fonts only as a separately scoped product/build decision.

entries.symptom: TypeScript did not preserve the selected profile narrowing inside the asynchronous worker closure.
entries.expected: The bounded harness compiles under repository strictness.
entries.actual: TS18048 reported that profile was possibly undefined inside worker().
repair_attempts: Bound the validated profile to an immutable runnableProfile before constructing workers.
entries.next_action: Retain strict compilation for harness entrypoints.

entries.symptom: The existing health-route test rejected direct process.env access added for deployment evidence context.
entries.expected: Healthz consumes centralized runtime/evidence context and does not inspect environment variables directly.
entries.actual: The initial route accessed VERCEL_ENV and VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA directly.
repair_attempts: Moved deployment evidence derivation into the API-owned readiness module and restored the route invariant.
entries.next_action: Keep environment parsing centralized outside public health routes.

entries.symptom: The first campaign failed before making a request because tsx emitted CommonJS and rejected top-level await.
entries.expected: The package script starts the harness under the repository module mode.
entries.actual: esbuild reported top-level await is unsupported with CJS output.
repair_attempts: Wrapped execution in an explicit async main with bounded error handling.
entries.next_action: Retain an executable harness smoke test in the performance campaign procedure.

entries.symptom: The default sandbox denied binding the isolated Next.js server to 127.0.0.1:3107.
entries.expected: A local production server is available for bounded read-only measurement.
entries.actual: listen returned EPERM; the approved localhost server subsequently started and was terminated after measurement.
repair_attempts: Started the same isolated server through the approved localhost boundary.
remaining_uncertainty: Local sandbox policy is not production runtime behavior.
entries.next_action: Use explicit local-runtime authorization and always terminate the measured server.

entries.symptom: The default sandbox could not connect to the approved localhost server and the harness recorded 100 status-599 samples.
entries.expected: Baseline samples reflect real HTTP responses from the isolated server.
entries.actual: All sandboxed requests failed before HTTP response; the approved rerun produced zero-error real responses. The failed samples were excluded from performance claims.
repair_attempts: Reran the unchanged harness with permission to connect only to the isolated localhost origin.
Changed threshold failure evaluation to return a failing process status before final measurements.
remaining_uncertainty: The local host does not represent preview or production network/runtime conditions.
entries.next_action: Treat status-599 as a failed campaign and retain only permission-valid response measurements for bounded claims.

entries.symptom: The preferred agent-browser CLI was not installed, and the in-app wrapper did not support the requested networkidle wait mode.
entries.expected: The exact local build receives browser rendering, overlay, console and navigation verification.
entries.actual: The CLI returned command not found; the in-app browser fallback connected successfully, used its supported DOM-content-ready wait, and completed all verification checks.
repair_attempts: Selected the available in-app browser control.
Replaced unsupported networkidle with the documented DOM-content-ready wait and explicit rendered-state checks.
remaining_uncertainty: The verification is local and not a preview/production browser observation.
entries.next_action: Use the in-app browser fallback on this host and repeat against the exact deployed candidate when available.
